reason: The cited evidence shows that DFT descriptors and physics-informed ML can accelerate property prediction (E2, E4), but none of the passages specifically address fracture toughness prediction, the HfNbTiVAl10 system, or the sufficiency of a sparse descriptor set for hierarchical heterostructures. E1 actually highlights low ductility in lightweight HEAs, which conflicts with the premise that toughness can be reliably predicted from the chosen descriptors.
premises: DFT-derived descriptors (elastic constants, misfit volumes, stacking fault/surface energies) capture essential physics for strength and toughness in HEAs
A sparse set of such descriptors suffices to train an accurate surrogate model
Physics-informed ML reduces computational cost vs. full DFT/CALPHAD while maintaining accuracy
Analytical surrogate models can be calibrated to predict fracture toughness from these descriptors
The approach is applicable to HfNbTiVAl10 with hierarchical heterostructure
